children: BMO Capital launched sweeping coverage across the retail sector. Analyst Kelly Crago issued both bull and bear ratings within the sector.
American Eagle Outfitters
at Market Perform rating and a $18 target price.

"AEO's story appears a tale of two brands, with very strong Aerie growth offsetting ongoing execution struggles at the larger American Eagle banner. We believe Aerie's momentum protects the downside to our estimates and the stock near-term, but without a durable comp recovery at AE, we see limited upside to guidance and struggle to underwrite FY27 earnings power."
Abercrombie & Fitch
started at Outperform with a $170 target price.

"ANF has pulled off one of the best softlines turnarounds in history. After a period of weaker growth, 2Q26 showed ANF is getting its groove back. A&F delivered its first positive comp in five quarters, and Hollister is seeing a back-to-school inflection."
Amer Sports
started at Outperform with a $38 target price.

"We believe Amer is one of the few compelling growth stories in consumer discretionary, with two global brands driving industry-leading sales growth. Arc’teryx is a proven, high-margin growth engine, while Salomon’s accelerating brand heat, U.S. distribution whitespace and still-small footwear business could drive meaningful upside to consensus estimates."
Academy Sports and Outdoors
started at a Market Perform rating and a $42 target price.

"After four years of struggling to drive positive comps under a favorable athletic category backdrop, we believe the path to consistent positive comps has grown even steeper now that the athletic category is slowing, making it difficult to underwrite ASO's long-term store growth runway."
Bath & Body Works
started at Market Perform and a $20 target price.

"We view new CEO Daniel Heaf's 'Consumer First Formula' plan as credible, and early wins, like the Hilary Duff Fruit Fusion launch, show the product engine can work. But FY26 marks the fifth straight year of sales declines, and we think righting the ship will take more time and investment, pressuring margins into FY27.
Birkenstock
started at Market Perform and a $35 target price.

"We see BIRK as a high-quality brand with a unique supply chain, industry-leading profitability, and strong full-price discipline. However, we believe top-line growth is maturing in BIRK's largest markets, leaving us more cautious relative to management's current growth outlook."
Carter's
started at an Outperform rating and a $40 target price.

"We believe investors are underestimating the company’s earnings recovery potential as new leadership restores brand relevance, accelerates traffic growth, improves wholesale mix, and benefits from lower tariffs."
Deckers Outdoor
started at Underperform and a $70 target price.

"Given a weakening athletic demand backdrop and many of DECK's athletic peers citing a highly promotional backdrop and cutting guidance, we are much more cautious on FY27/FY28E EPS at $7.18/$7.39 (versus consensus $7.52/$8.30) on a weaker HOKA outlook."
Dick's Sporting Goods
started at Underperform and a $110 target price.

"After years of strong performance and market share gains, we believe DKS faces more challenging category trends ahead and a messy turnaround as a multi-year shift away from athletic footwear takes hold. We see Foot Locker (FL) losing money again in FY27 and the core Dick's banner is no longer immune to a decelerating category, especially as it laps World Cup tailwinds next year."
Gap
started at Market Perform with a $23 target price.

"GAP's story runs through Old Navy, the company's largest banner, which stumbled badly in 1H26 and now heads into a pivotal 2H26 under new leadership. Until that business proves it can execute, it is tough to give credit for strong momentum at the Gap brand or underwrite the bull case for FY27 EPS."
Lululemon
started at Underperform with a $70 target price.

"After a decade-long run as one of the biggest winners in athletic, LULU now faces a business in free fall, with demand cracking across both the Americas/China and a premium margin structure that is completely unwinding."
Nike
started at Underperform with a $30 target price.

"Nike remains the largest, most important athletic brand despite recent challenges. CEO Elliott Hill is tasked with returning NKE to its former glory, a prospect that faces big challenges. Slowing lifestyle demand, a China distribution reset, and structurally lower margins push a fully recovered ~$3.00 EPS out to FY31."
On Holding
started at Market Perform with a $28 target price.

"While we believe ONON still has opportunities to grow, the next phase of growth looks more challenging, as management targets a scale only few athletic brands have achieved, against a more difficult demand backdrop."
Steve Madden
started at Outperform and a $60 target price.

"SHOO is in the early innings of what we view as the first fashion-footwear cycle in over a decade, with the company uniquely positioned to chase accelerating demand. Kurt Geiger adds a second underappreciated growth lever, bringing premium accessories exposure, U.S. distribution runway and margin upside."
Ulta Beauty
started at Market Perform and a $580 target price.
"We view ULTA as a high-quality market share leader in the U.S. beauty category, with an attractive/durable mid-single-digit sales and double-digit EPS growth algorithm."
Urban Outfitters
started at Market Perform and an $80 price target.

"We like URBN's portfolio of well-positioned, fashion-forward brands and its strong recent execution, with operating margin crossing 10% for the first time since 2015. But with shares trading in line with their historical multiple and near-term choppiness at Anthropologie (42% of sales) clouding the upside, we see a balanced risk/reward."
Victoria's Secret
started at Market Perform with an $80 target price.

"The Victoria's Secret and PINK turnaround is real and still has room to run, but following the stock's meaningful re-rating over the past year, we believe much of that recovery is now reflected in the shares."

title: Amer Sports, Steve Madden, and Carter's stand out in BMO's sweeping retail sector coverage
